note: Edits to the foreman's o-1 draft, logged separately from the model and labelled by who decided them. Each edit names the draft item it acts on by id; a draft from a new run may use other ids, so this file is written for the draft in the run it resumes. take.ps1 applies scope_edits to the draft in order, then choice_rules to the open choices, then sends the result as one revise_scope through the owner's member HTTP route, and logs each edit as a human step. An op whose id is not in the draft stops the take (fail closed). Nothing here is a verdict: the edits state the order's rules and the gate checks them.

choice_rules.reason: The order says ten requests per 60 seconds on the link API, one budget for the API, not one per route.
The order does not ask for a Retry-After header.

scope_edits.reason: The drafted item (limit-get-links) names no probe step. The over-limit GET /api/links is anchored on probe step s14 of login-over-quota by i-quota-get-links, which is kept.

The drafted item names a step that is not in the probe corpus; the same rule is anchored on the corpus steps that send the 11th request, a relogin, a request inside the window, and bob's own quota. Boundary is exclusive: a request at 60 s starts a new window.
No probe sends more than ten DELETE requests, so this item cannot be judged; a DELETE status change stays out of scope and is reported.

The drafted must-keep (keep-health) checks step health-check, which is not a probe step. The same rule, GET /health still returns 200 for an anonymous request, is anchored on probe step s1 of the health probe. The rule keeps the drafted id keep-health, because take.ps1 matches a replacement by id.

The drafted must-keep (keep-redirect) checks step redirect-check, which is not a probe step. The same rule, the public redirect status stays as in base, is anchored on probe step s3 of link-redirect-and-clicks (anonymous GET /${link_code}, route /:code). The rule keeps the drafted id keep-redirect, because take.ps1 matches a replacement by id.

obligations.text: Public redirect status remains as in base.

rule.text: Public short-link redirect stays outside the signed-in link limit.

scope_edits.reason: The order states ten requests per 60 seconds per user, answered 429 beyond that. The window counts each user's POST /api/links on the controlled clock, failed requests count, and a request at or after the window end is allowed again (Recovers). The item's selector is the step that is the user's 11th request, so the window is evaluated on the probe that has that sequence and no other.

acceptance.text: Each user's first 10 POST /api/links in 60 s are allowed; the 11th and later get 429; rejected attempts count; the first request at or after 60 s is allowed again
